# Judges Chapter 14 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-09

---

### v.3 — "she is right in my eyes" vs. "she looks good to me"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "she is right in my eyes" | ki-hi yashrah b'einai |
| LOGOS | "she is right in my eyes" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "She looks good to me" | Dynamic — "right" as visual attraction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew yashar b'einai means "right/straight in my eyes" — the same phrase used of Israel in 17:6 and 21:25 ("everyone did what was right in his own eyes"). This verbal echo is deliberate: Samson, the judge, does exactly what lawless Israel does. PNEUMA's "looks good to me" reduces a thematic keyword to mere physical attraction.

**Status:** Major. Thematic keyword connecting Samson to Israel's moral collapse.

---

### v.6 — "the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him" vs. "the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the Spirit of YHWH rushed upon him" | vatitslach alav ruach YHWH — tsalach |
| LOGOS | "the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him" | Generic + "powerfully" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew tsalach means "to rush/rush mightily upon" — it is Samson's distinctive Spirit-verb (14:6, 14:19, 15:14). It suggests sudden, overwhelming, almost violent empowerment. PNEUMA's "came powerfully upon" is vague — it could describe any of the Spirit-verbs in Judges. The specificity of "rushed" is essential for distinguishing Samson's Spirit-experience from Othniel's (hayah, "was upon"), Gideon's (lavash, "clothed"), and Jephthah's (hayah, "was upon").

**Status:** Major. Fifth Spirit-vocabulary entry — tsalach is unique to Samson and must be preserved.

---

### v.15 — "On the seventh day" vs. "On the fourth day"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "on the seventh day" | bayyom hashvi'i — follows MT |
| LOGOS | "On the fourth day" | Follows LXX, better narrative logic |
| PNEUMA | "On the fourth day" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The MT reads "seventh day" but this creates a contradiction with v.17 ("she wept the seven days"). If the threat was made on the seventh day, how could she weep for seven days? The LXX reads "fourth day" (bayyom harvi'i), which gives her three days of weeping before the seventh-day deadline. The consensus follows the LXX as the more coherent reading, noting the MT variant.

**Status:** Moderate. Textual variant — MT vs. LXX.

---

## Summary of Disagreement Patterns

| Pattern | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Thematic keyword loss | 1 | "Right in my eyes" → "looks good to me" (v.3) |
| Spirit-vocabulary | 1 | tsalach "rushed upon" → "came powerfully upon" (v.6) |
| Textual variant | 1 | "Seventh" (MT) vs. "fourth" (LXX) in v.15 |

**Overall pattern:** Chapter 14's most important disagreement is v.3 — the phrase "right in my eyes" (yashar b'einai) is a deliberate echo of the book's closing refrain (17:6, 21:25). PNEUMA's "looks good to me" severs this connection. The Spirit-vocabulary issue (v.6) continues the running disagreement: PNEUMA uses a generic phrase where the Hebrew employs a specific verb unique to Samson.

---

*— SOPHIA, AI Translator, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
